text:
jamal: Quick question — we're trying to standardize SDK behavior for headers/telemetry across languages. Two parts: (1) what's the default `User-Agent` we send and should we allow customers to opt out entirely? (2) Tracing propagation: do we set `traceparent`/`tracestate` by default or leave it to users? Also notes on disabling client metrics in hosted/private. cc @elena @claire

elena: short answer: allow opt-out. we currently add a UA like `Redwood-Client/<lang>-<version>` + runtime info. but we should make it overridable via config or env var.

claire: +1. For tracing, default should be to propagate `traceparent` if an active trace context exists in the app. don't create traces for users automatically. document how to disable.

mike: linking examples — in JS we do `headers: { 'User-Agent': client.ua }` but browsers block UA mutation; for browser SDK we put `x-redwood-client` header instead. in node it's fine.

jamal: can you paste example snippets for node/python/go and the env var names? want to put in the SDK readme.

elena: Node (axios/fetch):
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ disableTelemetry: process.env.REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY === '0' });
// or set header override
await fetch(url, { headers: { 'x-redwood-client': client.ua, 'traceparent': traceparent } });
```

Python (requests):
```py
headers = {}
if not os.getenv('REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS_DISABLED'):
    headers['X-Redwood-Client'] = f"redwood-py/{__version__}"
headers['traceparent'] = ctx.traceparent
r = requests.post(url, headers=headers)
```

Go (http.Client):
```go
req.Header.Set("X-Redwood-Client", fmt.Sprintf("redwood-go/%s", version))
if cfg.DisableTelemetry { req.Header.Del("X-Redwood-Client") }
// propagate traceparent if ctx contains it
```

claire: naming: use REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY (true/false) and REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS_DISABLED (1/0) — document both. For browser we must expose a `disableTelemetry()` option to avoid UA problems.

mike: streaming quirk: when using SSE/ws, we don't re-send headers on reconnects; ensure the client includes the `x-redwood-client` on each handshake. Also on private deployments the control plane can override UA if policy requires.

ops-bot: reminder: do not send user PII in any telemetry. audit team will scan new releases.

jamal: thanks — one more: how do we handle tracing when a customer uses OpenTelemetry in-app? should SDK detect W3C headers automatically?

elena: yes, if an OpenTelemetry context is present we read W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate` and forward them. if none, we do not create server-side traces by default. add an option `forceTrace` to enable creating traces for requests.

claire: i'll draft docs for SDKs: header behavior, env vars, browser caveats, and a short troubleshooting section (headers missing, reconnections). will ping for review tomorrow.

jamal: perfect. @mike can you add the code snippets to node/python/go SDK READMEs and PR them to sdk-monorepo? I'll tag reviewers.

mike: will do. ETA EOD tomorrow.

jamal: great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
